      FLIGHT MANUAL / REFERENCE

      Your seat. Your mission.

      Direct a launch

      Open the command console with C. Complete the eight systems and six station votes. Configure the vehicle, then start the countdown. A late failed check holds at T−10; an ignition interlock safes the pad.

      Move through the world

      1 Mission control · 2 Commander · 3 Pad camera. Drag to look. Click a physical control, or aim at it and press E to interact. In the pad's FREE camera use WASD, Q/R down/up, and Shift to move faster.

      Follow every vehicle

      Press S or 3 VIEWS for simultaneous Starship, booster and capsule cameras. Select a pane label to make it the main view. SPACEPORT opens the traffic overview. The five distant sites fly fictional scheduled departures and arrivals at real-time speed, independently of mission acceleration.

      Fly and respond

      Space pauses; H holds/resumes the count; F toggles fullscreen; M toggles audio. Throttle and pitch are in Vehicle. Faults and fictional escape are in Training. Eject at any flight phase with the escape control; the view follows the capsule so you can see its escape motors and descent. Press P or Deploy Parachutes to arm the canopies. Abort cuts thrust; it does not guarantee survival. Choose BOOSTER or STARSHIP in the camera controls to watch recovery; ENGINES looks directly beneath the selected rocket.

      Simulation boundaries

      The 120 m reference stack uses 33 booster and six ship engines. Its variable-mass model includes gravity, atmosphere, drag, staging and guided return. The default profile reserves propellant for a short return to Starbase: booster to LZ-01 and ship to the launch tower. These are illustrative recovery scenarios, not reproductions of operational SpaceX trajectories. The model omits 6-DOF dynamics, detailed thermal/structural response and Earth rotation.

      Mission control, the crew interior, station workflow and optional ejectable capsule are concepts. Real Starship has no publicly documented ejectable capsule. This is independent software, with no connection to SpaceX or real launch systems.

      Cinematic failures

      Vehicle impacts ignite at the collision location. Major failures produce a flash, turbulent fireball, ground shockwave, metal debris, smoke and a rolling explosion sound. In Training, inject structural breakup during flight to rehearse an airborne rupture. The effects use real-time pacing even during accelerated flight; pause freezes them. Camera shock can be turned off in Settings. These are authored cinematic effects, not a blast-damage calculation.

      How it runs

      Your browser runs the flight model on the CPU and renders the scene on your GPU using WebGL. All players have independent local missions. The site serves static files; no cloud gaming session or account is needed. Balanced graphics, adaptive resolution and compressed textures keep the default lighter. Sound starts after a user interaction. Music is composed procedurally; narration uses available device voices.
